cases.name: row
cases.when: layout is "table" -- the wide layout, where the row renders as <tr role="row"> inside Table's grid
cases.reason: Every requirement that applies to a row in this shape is a clause of the `grid` pattern Table binds: the row role, the roving tab stop across the cells, and the Enter that activates the row all live on the <table> and are recorded there. The row owns none of them, which is why binding an interactive pattern here would claim a route this element does not have -- the same reason Tab binds `none` under `tabs` and SideNavItem binds `none` under `navigation`. A <tr> also cannot become a <button>: a button may not be a child of <tbody>, and the row's actions cell draws the consumer's real buttons inside it.

cases.name: card-interactive
cases.when: layout is "card" and `interactive` is true -- below --bp-md the row renders as a <div>, which CAN carry role="button"

cases.name: card-inert
cases.when: layout is "card" and `interactive` is false -- the default, and nothing obliges a consumer to change it
cases.reason: With `interactive` false the card is a <div> with no role, no tab stop and no activation. There is nothing to press, so no interactive pattern applies to it.
